Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30 16:00 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Sam (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood CSM), Lina (Meridian Head of ML Ops), Owen (CTO), Maya (Platform Eng), Ravi (SRE), Janelle (Procurement)

Summary: quick QBR/health check after Nov production spike, look at cost drivers and next steps for a Dedicated pilot.

[00:00] Sam Carter: hey everyone, thanks for joining, hope folks can hear me ok. quick check, audio ok?
[00:06] Lina Park: yeah good here, thanks Sam. we pulled together the ops folks since the spike last week raised a few questions.
[00:12] Owen Delgado: morning all. we want clarity on whether this is an infra/config issue or something about the model profile.
[00:18] Priya Nair: thanks, yeah we'll run through what we see on our side and propose mitigations. first, can we confirm the spike was Nov 18th between 02:00 and 05:00 UTC?
[00:28] Maya Chen: correct those were our heavy batch inference windows from the ETL pipeline, but unusual — we had a 2x QPS increase and some long tails.
[00:36] Ravi Singh: latency climbed from ~120ms p50 to 850ms p90 for the generative endpoint. error rates low but timeouts increased.
[00:45] Priya Nair: ok, initial read — most likely KV cache misses combined with some request bursts that bypassed batching. there was also a deployment change on your side on Nov 17th that increased sequence length for a subset of calls, is that right?
[00:58] Maya Chen: yep we changed prompt templates to include more context for triage; average tokens per request went from ~220 to ~760 for a small subset.
[01:05] Sam Carter: that sequence length jump will affect kernel selection and cost. it also reduces how effectively the runtime can pack requests into batches.
[01:12] Lina Park: ok so is the recommendation just smaller prompts or are there platform knobs we can flip?
[01:18] Priya Nair: both. short-term: enable prefix KV caching for repeated context, set conservative max-batch latency to prioritise p50, and use request shaping to smooth bursts. medium-term: Dedicated pools or reserved capacity to avoid noisy-neighbor effects during sudden spikes.
[01:28] Owen Delgado: how big is the cost delta if we move to Dedicated? we have seasonal spikes but want predictable spend.
[01:36] Sam Carter: we'll produce a break-even analysis. initial ballpark: at your sustained baseline of 1200 qps/day the Dedicated plan starts to look 10-18% cheaper after steady-state commit, but it depends on burst patterns and ability to auto-burst.
[01:47] Lina Park: can we get a model that shows our current A-B usage patterns? the November billing was about 37% higher than forecast which triggered a lot of questions.
[01:55] Diego Ramos: yes we pulled your aggregated token counts and cost per route — we'll attach a detailed sheet. we want to show cost drivers: longer sequences, retries, and non-optimal batching.
[02:03] Maya Chen: reruns of some older jobs also contributed; our scheduler re-tried failed jobs during the window.
[02:10] Priya Nair: sounds like a mix of workload shape and retries. for retries we recommend idempotency keys and backoff so they don't thundering herd.
[02:18] Ravi Singh: on security — Janelle wanted to reiterate SOC2 evidence and KMS integration tests before any Dedicated pilot. what's the current state?
[02:26] Janelle Ortiz: yes procurement needs a package we can review, and we need SSO/SAML mapping to our IdP, plus audit log retention options.
[02:34] Sam Carter: we have SOC2 type II docs and the KMS integration guide. for Private/Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via KMS and HSM options; we'll share the security pack after this call.
[02:44] Janelle Ortiz: also data residency — some data must remain in the EU region for regulatory reasons. can Dedicated be provisioned in eu-west-1?
[02:52] Priya Nair: yes we can provision regionally; we'll note capacity lead times. Dedicated in eu-west typically needs a 3–4 week lead time for capacity reservations.
[02:59] Owen Delgado: what's the rollback strategy if Dedicated pilot causes regressions? eg. hallucination rate or latency regressions.
[03:07] Diego Ramos: recommended approach: canary 5–10% traffic, compare latency and quality on held-out evals, automatic fallback policy to hosted model variant with compatibility layer. we'll include A/B rollout steps in the runbook.
[03:18] Maya Chen: can Redwood run an out-of-the-box benchmark using our sample prompts? that would help size Dedicated right.
[03:24] Priya Nair: absolutely; Priya: I'll run a 24-hour benchmark with your payload shape. we'll test with current prompt lengths and with the trimmed variants to see sensitivity.
[03:33] Lina Park: perfect. and can we surface token-level cost by route? procurement wants that for chargebacks.
[03:39] Sam Carter: yes, Console provides per-route token cost, and we can export CSV for your finance system. we'll attach that.
[03:46] Ravi Singh: a question about caching — you mentioned 'KV cash' earlier in the doc — sorry, typo i think — do you mean KV cache? how much lift is there to enable it for us?
[03:55] Priya Nair: yes KV cache — enabling prefix caching is configuration only; we might need changes if your context shapes are dynamic. for repeated contexts it's very effective, often reducing token generation by 20-40% and improving p90s.
[04:06] Owen Delgado: any implications for privacy/reg compliance when caching?
[04:10] Priya Nair: we can scope cache keys to non-sensitive prefixes, and for private deployments customers can use local-only cache and encrypt with KMS. we'll document safe patterns.
[04:20] Janelle Ortiz: procurement also flagged termination and data purge clauses for Dedicated contracts — we'll push legal language we need.
[04:26] Sam Carter: understood, we'll have legal coordinate; Diego will be the point for compliance package.
[04:33] Diego Ramos: will do. also recommend creating an internal runbook page with roles — who owns rollbacks, who escalates to Redwood SEs. we'll draft a runbook template.
[04:43] Maya Chen: for the pilot we also want end-to-end observability — token latency, KV hit-rate, per-request kernel path. are those metrics surfaced?
[04:52] Priya Nair: yes Console exposes token-level latency, model kernel telemetry, KV hit-rate, and batching efficiency. we can add tracing hooks into your service to correlate traces.
[05:00] Owen Delgado: great. final question: if we keep Hosted and just tune, could we avoid Dedicated? what's the recommended threshold?
[05:07] Sam Carter: recommendation: if your monthly committed tokens exceed X (we'll compute exact from your export) and predictability of SLA is important, Dedicated makes sense. otherwise heavy tuning + autoscaling policies and better batching can keep Hosted viable, but costs vary with burstiness.
[05:21] Lina Park: ok that's helpful. next steps recap?
[05:24] Diego Ramos: Redwood to run benchmark (Priya) and share results, Sam to share cost spreadsheet, Diego to draft ops runbook, Maya to share traffic traces, Meridian to review security pack and nominate pilot team.
[05:36] Janelle Ortiz: we'll review legal clauses and circle back to Sam.
[05:40] Sam Carter: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts by next week and propose calendar invites for the pilot kickoff.
[05:47] Owen Delgado: thanks all, appreciate the quick turnaround on the benchmark.
[05:50] Lina Park: thanks, speak soon.
